issues.line_text: Waited for recognition to crack through.
issues.description: Eleanor watching for Josh to RECOGNIZE/REMEMBER the tower room. This is investigator language, not predator language. Predators watch for FEAR/VULNERABILITY. This pattern was flagged in Session 6 (January 12, 2026) and fixed in other chapters (lines 5997, 6009, 7909, etc.).

issues.line_text: Nothing. No recognition. Still hiding. Even from himself.
issues.description: Eleanor's internal monologue uses 'recognition' (investigator term) and 'hiding even from himself' (reveals she knows about his dissociative condition). This is too investigative and reveals her certainty about his fugue states before Act 3.
issues.fix: Nothing. Just confusion in his face. Still oblivious.
issues.rationale: Removes 'recognition' language and the dissociative hint. 'Oblivious' fits predator mindset (he doesn't fear her yet) without revealing she knows about his condition. Matches the fix applied at line 6009.

issues.line_text: The tower room. He found it and felt nothing. No recognition. No unease. He has no idea. He stands right on top of the truth and doesn't see it.
issues.description: Eleanor's journal entry uses 'recognition' again and 'stands right on top of the truth' which reveals she knows a specific truth about the tower room (that he was there in 2020 as Marcus). This is investigator language exposing her certainty.
issues.fix: The tower room. He found it and felt nothing. No fear. No unease. He has no idea what's coming. He stands where it happened and doesn't feel a thing.
issues.rationale: Changes 'recognition' to 'fear' (predator watching). 'Stands where it happened' is vague (could mean anything threatening) vs. 'stands on top of the truth' (too specific/investigative). 'What's coming' maintains predatory threat tone.

issues.line_text: "Someone I lost," I whispered. "Someone who deserved better."
issues.description: While Eleanor is revealing emotion here (which is fine in a charged confrontation), the phrasing 'someone I lost' + 'deserved better' leans toward grief/memorial language rather than predatory deflection. Not critical, but could be slightly more guarded.
issues.fix: "Someone who mattered," I whispered. "Someone who deserved better than what happened here."
issues.rationale: Maintains emotional authenticity without the 'I lost' phrasing that tips toward personal grief. 'Someone who mattered' + 'what happened here' keeps it more about the place/event than personal loss, while still showing vulnerability that makes Josh soften.
